questions.q: What does a Transform Map decide that a Data Source does not?
options: What file format the source data arrives in
Where the external data physically comes from, such as a file or a database
The recurrence schedule for when an import runs
Which staging columns become which target fields, and whether a row should insert or update
questions.explain: The Data Source only governs how data gets into staging; the Transform Map governs what happens to it after that.

questions.q: Why doesn't a source column name like `emp_email` need to match the target field name `email`?
options: Because coalesce fields are exempt from needing any mapping at all
Because staging tables and target tables always share identical column names
Because ServiceNow renames all columns automatically to match the target table
Because field mapping explicitly translates one staging column to one target field, by hand
questions.explain: Field mapping is exactly the layer where source and target naming differences get reconciled, pair by pair.

questions.q: What does setting a coalesce field on a Transform Map actually control?
options: How often a Scheduled Import runs
Whether a staged row updates an existing target record or inserts a new one, based on a matching value
Which columns appear in the auto-created staging table
Which file format the Data Source accepts
questions.explain: Coalesce checks for an existing match on the chosen field; a match updates the record, no match inserts a new one.

questions.q: What commonly goes wrong if a Transform Map has no coalesce field set for a recurring import?
options: The staging table refuses to accept any new rows
ServiceNow automatically assigns a coalesce field with no admin input needed
The import fails immediately and no data loads at all
Running the same import again creates duplicate records instead of updating existing ones
questions.explain: Without coalesce, the transform has no way to recognize an existing record, so every rerun just inserts new rows.

questions.q: When is a Run Script transform the right tool instead of a plain 1:1 field mapping?
options: Whenever any field mapping exists at all, even simple 1:1 copies
When a target field needs logic beyond a straight copy, such as combining columns or a conditional lookup
Only when the Data Source type is JDBC
Only when no coalesce field has been configured
questions.explain: Run Script handles computed or conditional field logic; simple field-to-field copies don't need it.
